messages:
maya: Prospect (large payer) requires VPC peering for POC. Asking for a short runbook we can hand to their infra team: steps, minimal TF, and secure API key handoff. Need to start this week.

diego: Runbook draft: 1) Confirm VPC CIDRs do not overlap. 2) Customer creates VPC Peering -> share peering_connection_id. 3) We accept the peering (manual accept for now). 4) Both sides add route entries for the specific app subnets -> peering id. 5) Update SGs: allow inbound TCP/443 from the peer app subnet CIDRs only. 6) NACLs: ensure ephemeral ports allowed for return traffic. 7) Test from a bastion: curl our control-plane IP/DNS.

nina: Minimal TF (customer side):
```
resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "peer" {
  vpc_id        = var.customer_vpc_id
  peer_vpc_id   = var.redwood_vpc_id
  peer_owner_id = var.redwood_account_id
}
resource "aws_route" "to_redwood" {
  route_table_id             = var.route_table_id
  destination_cidr_block     = var.redwood_service_cidr
  vpc_peering_connection_id  = aws_vpc_peering_connection.peer.id
}
```
Replace vars with real IDs. Remember reciprocal route in our route table.

maya: Key delivery options if PrivateLink is not allowed?

nina: Short-lived POC key (24-48h) we can push into their vault via a presigned single-use upload link, or share via their vault integration. All key issues get an audit-id. We recommend vault push over email.

diego: Quick validation commands for infra: 1) `curl -v https://<control-plane-ip>/health` from their bastion -> expect 200. 2) `openssl s_client -connect <control-plane-ip>:443 -servername control.redwood.ai` -> cert CN check. 3) If 403 -> check SG CIDR and route.

infra-bot: Ticket POC-6210 created. Owner: nina. ETA: 48h to accept peering after request received.

maya: I'll send this one-pager and ask for CIDRs + peering id. If they insist on DNS-friendly names, suggest Dedicated or Private since peering doesn't provide private DNS mapping.

diego: Good call. Flag SOW option for Dedicated if they push back on NAT/allowlist.
